references.text: Describes the consequence of eating a peace offering while unclean—the person shall be cut off from their people, the same penalty as in Leviticus 22:3
Warning that the Israelites must keep away from their uncleanness so they do not die by making the Lord's dwelling place unclean
The one who touches a dead body and does not cleanse themselves makes the Lord's tabernacle unclean and shall be cut off from Israel
Men who were unclean because of a dead body could not celebrate Passover at the appointed time—uncleanness prevented participation in holy acts
Continuation of the same passage elaborating on various forms of uncleanness that prevent priests from eating the holy offerings
Aaron and his sons shall wear the holy garments when they enter the tent of meeting, so they do not incur guilt and die
The same expression 'shall be cut off from their people' is used for the one who does not bring their offering to the tent of meeting
